## Slides and markers

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}
print(markers.ls[select.slides], quote=F)
```

\bigskip

Marker groups

- T cell: CD3 CD4 CD8 CD69 CD279 Foxp3
- Neutrophil: CD15
- Dendritic cells: CD11c CD123 
- Macrophage: CD68
- NK cells: CD56. This marker is expressed on both NK and nerve fibers, need to check if the staining on the latter affects the NK cell count.


The key markers are: CD11c CD123 CD3 CD15 CD56 CD68. There are 13 lesion biopsies in total. We will focus on lesion biopsies with the key markers data.

The CD68 antibody stained the epidermis of some tissues. CD68_raw.png is the raw image, and CD68.png is the processed image with reduced epidermis brightness to improve quality of segmentation. 

Some lesion biopsies have multiple sections. The following choices of slides are made: 

- AS/AS1_Les
- CF/CF1_Les
- CJ/CJ1_Les
- DD/DD1_Les
- EB/EB_Les
- JK/JK1_Les
- JM/JM1_Les
- JT/JT_Les
- LD/LD_Les
- LG/LG2_Les
- LM/LM_Les
- LS/LS2_Les
- SK/SK2_Les 

The only exceptions are

- For CF CD68, CF5 is used instead of CF1 for better quality.




## Density curves

Number of cells per 100x100 um2 tissue as a function of distance to skin.
The curves are smoothed over histograms and each bin in the histogram represents a 100 um interval. 
Adding up the counts from all the bins gives the number of cells in tissue of 100 um in width.

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}
cat("\\begin{figure}[H]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{output/figures/compare_normal_lesion_dist2skin.png}\\end{figure}\n")
cat("\\begin{figure}[H]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{output/figures/compare_normal_lesion_dist2DEJ.png}\\end{figure}\n")
```



Comparing the first two rows in the first column, we see that the ratio of the area under the curve across both epi and dermis between red and blue(ulcerative and intact) is about 1 for CD3/CF and 1/3 for CD3/DD. This suggests that CD3 is depleted in lesion in DD, but not in CF.

Compare lesion with normal in CD15/CF, we see that the lesion peak is shifted to the left compared to the normal peak. This pattern is more clear in CF than in DD. We don't see this pattern for CD3.
    
\newpage

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}
cat("\\begin{figure}[H]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\textwidth]{output/figures/compare_markers.png}\\end{figure}\n")
```

That the CD15 dist2skin peak in DD/lesion is near skin while the corresponding dist2DEJ peak is near DEJ is due to the fact that the DEJ line is very curvy.

## Scatterplots of Shedding rate and counts and densities

Different biopsy samples or even different slices from the same biopsy sample may have different amount of lesion tissues. Some completely lack lesion.



```{r, echo=FALSE}
# count.tables is a list. each element is named after a slide name, e.g. AS1_Les
# count.tables$AS1_Les is a list of 3 elements: DEJ500, DEJ1000, DEJInf
# count.tables$AS1_Les[['DEJ500']] is a list with 4 columns: sizes, counts, densities, reg.densities
a="CD3"
xx=c("DEJ500", "DEJ1000", "DEJInf"); names(xx)=xx

counts=lapply(xx, function (x) {
  out = as.data.frame(mysapply(select.slides, function (s) count.tables[[s]][[x]]$counts[,a]))
  cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
        out,
        total=rowSums(out))
})

densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
  out = as.data.frame(mysapply(select.slides, function (s) count.tables[[s]][[x]]$densities[,a]))
  cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
        out,
        total=rowSums(out))
})

reg.densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
  out = as.data.frame(mysapply(select.slides, function (s) count.tables[[s]][[x]]$reg.densities[,a]))
  cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
        out,
        total=rowSums(out))
})

# kable(countsDEJ500, caption="Counts and shedding rate (SR). DI: dermis intact; DU: dermis ulcerative; EI: epidermis intact; EU: epidermis ulcerative.")
```

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.height=9, fig.width=7}
# scatterplot of shedding_rate vs cnt_total

par(mfrow=c(4,3))
reduce_margin()

# plot total cell count of dermis/epidermis intact and ulcerative
ylim=c(0,max(counts$DEJInf$total))
for (x in rev(xx)) {
  with(counts[[x]], {
    plot(SR, total, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Total cells ({x})"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
    legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(total[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
  })
}

# plot densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
ylim=NULL
for (x in rev(xx)) {
  with(densities[[x]], {
    plot(SR, DI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Densities ({x}) DI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
    legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(DI[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
  })
}

# plot regularized densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
ylim=NULL
for (x in rev(xx)) {
  with(reg.densities[[x]], {
    plot(SR, DI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Reg Densities ({x}) DI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
    legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(DI[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
  })
}

# plot densities for epidermis intact, this does not depend on the DEJ500/DEJ1000/DEJInf
ylim=NULL
with(densities[[1]], {
  plot(SR, EI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Densities DI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
  legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(EI[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
})

ylim=NULL
with(reg.densities[[1]], {
  plot(SR, EI, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Reg Densities EI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
  legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(EI[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
})


```

DI: dermis intact; EI: epidermis intact; DEJ500: dermis up to 500 um below DEJ; DEJ1000: dermis up to 1000 um below DEJ; DEJInf: all dermis.
R2* is computed without AS1_Les, which has the highest shedding rate.


```{r, echo=FALSE}
# count.tables.2 is a list. each element is named after a slide name, e.g. AS1_Les
# count.tables.2$AS1_Les is a list of 3 elements: Skin1000, SkinInf
# count.tables.2$AS1_Les[['skin1000']] is a list with 4 columns: sizes, counts, densities, reg.densities
a="CD3"
xx=c("Skin1000", "SkinInf"); names(xx)=xx

counts=lapply(xx, function (x) {
  out = as.data.frame(mysapply(select.slides, function (s) count.tables.2[[s]][[x]]$counts[,a]))
  cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
        out,
        total=rowSums(out))
})

densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
  out = as.data.frame(mysapply(select.slides, function (s) count.tables.2[[s]][[x]]$densities[,a]))
  cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
        out,
        total=rowSums(out))
})

reg.densities=lapply(xx, function (x) {
  out = as.data.frame(mysapply(select.slides, function (s) count.tables.2[[s]][[x]]$reg.densities[,a]))
  cbind(SR = severity$Shedding.rate[match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial)], 
        out,
        total=rowSums(out))
})

# kable(countsskin500, caption="Counts and shedding rate (SR). DI: dermis intact; DU: dermis ulcerative; EI: epidermis intact; EU: epidermis ulcerative.")
```

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=4.7}
# scatterplot of shedding_rate vs cnt_total

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
reduce_margin()

# plot total cell count of dermis/epidermis intact and ulcerative
ylim=c(0,max(counts$SkinInf$total))
for (x in rev(xx)) {
  with(counts[[x]], {
    plot(SR, total, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Total cells ({x})"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
    legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(total[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
  })
}

# plot regularized densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
ylim=NULL
for (x in rev(xx)) {
  with(reg.densities[[x]], {
    plot(SR, I, xlab="Shedding rate", main=glue("Reg Densities ({x}) I"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim)
    legend("topright", legend=paste("R2*=", round(summary(lm(I[-1] ~ SR[-1]))$r.squared, 3)), bty="n")
  })
}


```

I: intact; Skin1000: up to 1000 um below skin; SkinInf: all depth.
R2* is computed without AS1_Les, which has the highest shedding rate.



## Count tables

For each slide, there are two tables, one for up to 500 um below DEJ and one for up to 1000 um below DEJ.
